cards.front: Defend to the Aufsichtsrat: why is the Neubewertungsreserve stripped from the Deckungsmasse in BOTH the Problemfall and the Extremfall, and by what DIFFERENT mechanics?

rubric.text: States it is OUT under both scenarios (net effect identical)
Extremfall mechanic: an explicit '− Neubewertungsreserve' deduction line
Problemfall mechanic: it never enters because Freies Kapital is defined net of it from the outset (NOT added back)
Rationale: volatile, scenario-correlated paper value, not hard loss-absorbing substance — can evaporate in the very stress tested

antiPoints: claims it is added back in the Problemfall because it was 'only removed in the Extremfall'
treats the Neubewertungsreserve as hard CET1 that can absorb loss
cards.modelAnswer: The Neubewertungsreserve is excluded from the cover under both scenarios because it is volatile, scenario-correlated fair-value paper rather than durable loss-absorbing substance — in the very stress we test it can evaporate. The mechanics differ: in the Extremfall it is an explicit '− Neubewertungsreserve' deduction line, whereas in the Problemfall it simply never enters, because Freies Kapital is defined as CET1 net of the Neubewertungsreserve from the outset. Either way the net effect is identical, so it must not be 'added back' in the Problemfall on the mistaken belief it was only removed in the Extremfall.

cards.front: Explain the IFRS/CRR-Rechnungskreis double-count avoidance: why does the Problemfall freier Überschuss ADD BACK expected risk costs, and why does the Extremfall add NO after-tax period surplus?

tags.risk: IFRS 9 double-count of EL and period profit

rubric.text: Under IFRS 9 the EL loss allowance already reduces equity / own funds
Adding expected risk costs back to the surplus prevents charging EL twice (once in the surplus, again as the excess/shortfall)

The after-tax period surplus is already in equity, captured by anrechenbare Eigenmittel in the Extremfall, so adding it again as 'next-year profit' double-counts — hence continuing-ops pre-tax + Gewinnvortrag only
Links to Module 5: capital carries UL only; EL lives in the Deckungsmasse

antiPoints: says IFRS banks are riskier and simply need a bigger buffer
claims IFRS forbids counting any surplus at all
cards.modelAnswer: Under IFRS 9 the expected-loss allowance already reduces equity and hence own funds. Because the excess/shortfall block nets EL against provisions a second time, the IFRS Problemfall adds the expected risk costs back to the budgeted Konzernüberschuss to avoid charging EL twice. In the Extremfall the period surplus after tax is likewise already inside equity, which the cover counts directly through anrechenbare Eigenmittel; adding a separate 'next-year after-tax profit' would double-count, so the Extremfall uses only profit from continuing operations pre-tax plus Gewinnvortrag. It is the same discipline as Module 5: capital carries unexpected loss only, while expected loss lives in the Deckungsmasse.

cards.front: Contrast Freies Kapital in the Problemfall vs the Extremfall, and justify why the Extremfall adds back the Abzugsposten Beteiligungen and includes nachrangiges Fremdkapital.

tags.risk: Freies Kapital — going vs gone concern

rubric.text: Problemfall = only the hard CET1 ABOVE the Eigenmittelerfordernis (incl. P2R & combined buffer), net of Neubewertungsreserve
Extremfall = anrechenbare Eigenmittel − Neubewertungsreserve + nachrangiges FK + Abzugsposten Beteiligungen (the full stack)
Going concern must keep the minimum intact (breaching it IS the failure event); the gone concern may use the whole stack incl. subordinated debt because the minimum no longer needs protecting
Abzugsposten Beteiligungen are added back because participation risk is captured separately as Beteiligungsrisiko (Module 11) — leaving them deducted would double-penalise

antiPoints: counts the regulatory minimum CET1 as loss-absorbing in the Problemfall
leaves participations deducted AND charges Beteiligungsrisiko, double-counting
cards.modelAnswer: In the Problemfall the bank is a going concern, so only the hard CET1 it holds above its Eigenmittelerfordernis (including the P2R and the combined buffer requirement), net of the Neubewertungsreserve, is free — the minimum itself cannot absorb loss because breaching it is the failure event. In the Extremfall it is a gone concern near liquidation, so the whole stack is available: anrechenbare Eigenmittel minus the Neubewertungsreserve, plus nachrangiges Fremdkapital (subordinated debt absorbs loss in liquidation), plus the Abzugsposten Beteiligungen added back. The add-back avoids double-penalising participations, whose risk is already captured separately as Beteiligungsrisiko in Module 11.
